To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
increased protein intake rate results in increased kidney mass and increased kidney function in mice.

increased dietary protein content is the factor that is responsible for increased kidney and liver mass in response to increased protein intake, while increased food and energy intake are the factors responsible for the increases in digestive tract and other organ mass.
increased food intake rate is associated with increases in stomach mass, while increased protein intake rate is associated in increased liver, kidney and stomach masses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of increased protein and energy intake on kidney size, structure and function in mice acclimated to different temperatures.
the effects of increased food and increased protein intake on organ mass and function in mice acclimated to different environmental temperatures.
the effects of increased protein and food intake on kidney size, function and nitrogen balance, and how these responses are modified by temperature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for mice on a high-protein diet, the increase in kidney size, and the associated increase in glomerular filtration rate, is primarily a response to the increased protein intake.
the increased protein intake, rather than the increased energy intake, is responsible for the increase in kidney mass and function.
increased protein intake rate is responsible for increased kidney and liver mass, while increases in energy intake rate are responsible for increases in stomach mass and digestive tract mass.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increased energy demand associated with cold acclimation results in an increase in protein intake, which in turn results in an increase of kidney size and function and an increase of liver size, which are all consistent with the idea that these organs are responding to the increased energy demand.
the increased protein intake is responsible for the increased kidney mass and filtration rate.

, in the cold-acclimate mice, the increased protein intake resulted in increases in nitrogen filtration rate that were accompanied by increases in glomerular filtration rate, and that the increase in glomerular filtrate volume resulted in increased kidney size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the increased protein intake associated with increased food intake may be the proximate stimulus for increases in kidney size and function in response to increased metabolic energy demand.

, while increased energy intake rate is associated with increases in digestive tract, liver, and kidney mass, it is the increased protein intake that results in the increase in nitrogen filtration rate and glomerular filtration rate.

increased food intake is not necessarily the cause of increased organ mass and function, and that increased food intake may not be the cause of increased protein intake, which in turn is the factor responsible for the increased organ mass and increased organ function observed in response to increased metabolic energy demand.
